questions.q: In React, what is a component?
options: A CSS file for one page
A reusable function that returns UI
A table in the app's database
A plugin installed in the browser

questions.q: How does a parent component pass data to a child component in React?
options: Through a global CSS class name
By editing the child's file at run time
Only through the page URL
Through props, e.g. <Price amount={499} />

questions.q: What is JSX?
options: HTML-like syntax written inside JavaScript
A JSON file format used by React
A new web browser from Meta
A tool that minifies CSS files

questions.q: Which HTTP method is usually used to submit a sign-up form that creates a new account?
options: GET
HEAD
POST
OPTIONS

questions.q: const [count, setCount] = useState(0); Which line correctly increases count by 1?
options: count = count + 1
count++
setCount(count + 1)
useState(count + 1)

questions.q: Why does React warn when items rendered from a list have no key prop?
options: Keys let React match items between renders and update the right ones
Keys make the items load faster from the server
Keys are needed so CSS can style each item
Lists show nothing on screen without keys

questions.q: When does loadOrders run in useEffect(() => { loadOrders(); }, [])?
options: On every single render
Never, because the array is empty
Only when the page is closed
Once, after the component first renders

questions.q: A component's useEffect starts setInterval to refresh a live price every 5 seconds. What else must the effect do?
options: Call setInterval again inside the render
Return a cleanup function that calls clearInterval
Declare the timer with var, not const
Wrap the setInterval call in try/catch

questions.q: A click handler calls setCount(count + 1) twice, but count goes up by only 1. Which change makes it go up by 2?
options: Call setCount(c => c + 1) twice
Call setCount(count + 1) three times
Change count directly, then re-render
Add 1 inside a useEffect as well

questions.q: A child component must change a value that its parent owns. What is the usual React pattern?
options: Child changes props.value directly
Child keeps a copy in a global variable
Parent passes a callback prop; the child calls it with the new value
Child reloads the page to refresh it

questions.q: Code does items.push(newItem); setItems(items); but the list on screen does not update. Why?
options: push() does not exist on JavaScript arrays
The same array is passed, so React sees no change; pass a new array
setItems must always be called twice
React state can hold only numbers and text

questions.q: What is a controlled input in React?
options: An input that has the disabled attribute
An input styled only with CSS classes
An input checked only by the server
An input whose value comes from state and changes through onChange

questions.q: What are useMemo and useCallback mainly used for?
options: Fetching data from an API on page load
Reusing a value or function across renders to skip work
Saving data into localStorage
Replacing useState in large apps

questions.q: A list of 5,000 products re-renders slowly on every key press in the search box. What is the best first step?
options: Add console.log calls inside every row
Rewrite all components as class components
Move the CSS rules into the JS files
Profile it, then memoise list rows and debounce the search

questions.q: Which hook reads a value shared through Context, such as the logged-in user?
options: useContext
useState
useRef
useId

questions.q: What does localStorage do in the browser?
options: Stores uploaded files on the web server
Caches only the CSS files of a site
Keeps small key–value data in the browser across reloads
Saves form data straight into a database

questions.q: Your React app calls api.example.in and the browser blocks it with a CORS error. Where is this usually fixed?
options: In React, by renaming the fetch function
By clearing the browser's cache
On the API server, by sending headers that allow your site's origin
By moving the script tag into the head

questions.q: Many users open your site on budget phones over slow 4G. Which change helps first load the most?
options: Compress and lazy-load images, and split the large JS bundle
Add two more web fonts for headings
Switch the photos to large PNG files
Load every script in the head without defer

questions.q: Which is the accessible way to build a clickable 'Pay now' control?
options: A <div> with only an onclick
A <span> styled to look like a button
An with an onclick
A <button> element

questions.q: What does [3, 10, 1].sort() return in JavaScript?
options: An error

questions.q: A button has class btn and id pay. The CSS has .btn { color: red } then #pay { color: green }. What colour is its text?
options: Green, because an id selector is more specific
Red, because that rule comes first
Red, because classes beat ids
Black, because the rules cancel out

questions.q: What does array.map(fn) return?
options: The same array, changed in place
Only the first item that matches fn
A new array with fn applied to each item
Always undefined

questions.q: What does await do inside an async function?
options: Freezes the whole browser tab until done
Pauses only that function until the Promise settles
Turns a Promise into a plain string
Sends the code to run on the server

task.title: Fix a buggy React cart summary component
task.brief: Below is a small React component for a shopping cart summary. Users report several problems (listed under the code). In 20 to 25 minutes: (1) list every bug or bad practice you find and explain why it is a problem, (2) write the corrected component, and (3) say briefly how the coupon should behave (for example, applied only once, total never below zero). No code is run; clear reasoning matters as much as the code.
key_points: The input has value but no onChange, so it is read-only; add onChange={e => setCoupon(e.target.value)}
if (coupon = "SAVE50") assigns instead of comparing; use ===
total is mutated directly; state must change via a setter (or derive the total)
useEffect has no dependency array so it runs after every render; use [items] or compute the total during render / useMemo
List items need a key prop, e.g. key={i.id}
Use a <button> instead of a clickable <div> for keyboard and screen-reader access
Coupon logic: apply once (track applied state), keep total from going negative, show a message for an invalid code

rubric.label: Bugs found and fixed
rubric.guide: 0 = finds none or fix still broken, 3 = finds input, comparison and state bugs, 5 = finds all main bugs and the fixed component works

rubric.label: React practice
rubric.guide: 0 = mutates state or misuses hooks, 3 = mostly right, 5 = correct state updates, sensible effect or derived value, keys, accessible button

rubric.label: Edge cases
rubric.guide: 0 = none, 3 = mentions one or two, 5 = handles coupon applied twice, empty cart, negative total and wrong codes

rubric.label: Explanation
rubric.guide: 0 = no reasons, 3 = brief or partly wrong, 5 = each problem explained clearly and simply
